Free courses · 5 puzzles so far · about 30 minutes

TCP to HTTPS, one request under a microscope

Trace a mobile request from opening the connection to authenticating the server, counting the first byte and understanding what packet loss changes.

Builds on Mobile system design, from a packet to an app.

Start learning Browse modules

Course outline

  • Module 1: Open, secure and reuse a connection4 puzzles

    Follow sequence numbers, missing bytes, TLS proof and a first-byte budget.

    1. Why TCP starts with three messages Follow the first exchange between a phone and a server. What has each side learned at every step?
    2. Where do the missing bytes go? Drop one range of bytes while a later range arrives. Predict what the receiver reports and what the application can read.
    3. Who proves the server’s identity? The phone can already exchange bytes. Work out what it must verify before trusting the peer with an application request.
    4. Where did the extra round trips go? Time one small request over a new connection, then reuse the connection and account for the difference.
    Check what you already know
  • Module 2: Share a connection under loss1 puzzles

    Compare delivery on HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 with the same two requests.

    1. Can a lost image slow a text response? Two responses share a connection. Change the transport and predict which response can keep moving after loss.
    Check what you already know

Final project

Explain a slow first response · Use a timing trace and a loss trace to decide whether to change the connection lifecycle, the server or the transport.

How the course works

Follow the mechanism, predict a change and check your answer. Optional depth is available from the same puzzle.

Every puzzle is open from this outline. The check at the end of a puzzle unlocks its next button and saves your progress in this browser.
